name: Attribute Reference
title: Attribute Reference Tables — Valid Values for All Dropdown Fields
preamble: Attribute Reference Tables — Valid Values for All Dropdown Fields
headers: Must be complied with. Non-compliance is a breach. Used for legislative, ISM and PSPF mandatory requirements.
Failure to comply creates an immediate, significant risk of data breach, system compromise or regulatory breach.
rows: Best practice. Strongly encouraged but not legally required. Used for ISO 27001 / NIST guidance.
Failure to comply creates a significant risk that is likely to be exploited or result in non-compliance.
Informational. Provides context or clarification. No compliance obligation.
Failure to comply creates a moderate risk. Exploitable but less likely or lower impact.
Failure to comply creates a minor risk. Unlikely to be exploited or limited impact if it is.
Controls implemented via technology (software, hardware, system configuration).
Exceptions are permitted subject to a formal process and approval.
Controls implemented via policy, process, training or governance.
No exceptions are permitted. This requirement must always be met. Usually reserved for legislative obligations.
Controls implemented via physical means (locks, barriers, access cards, CCTV).
Exceptions are permitted only under specific conditions (e.g. technical impossibility), with compensating controls.
Controls arising directly from legislative or contractual obligations.
Requirement has been identified but not yet formally reviewed or approved.
Monitored automatically in real-time via SIEM, dashboards or automated controls.
Requirement is formally approved and in force.
Reviewed by the SOC or system administrator on a monthly basis.
Requirement is being reviewed (e.g. due to a regulatory change or incident).
Reviewed quarterly, typically by the CISO team or internal audit.
Requirement has been replaced by a newer version. Retained for audit trail.
Requirement no longer applies and has been formally retired.
Reviewed once per year as part of the annual PSPF self-assessment or internal audit cycle.
Reviewed when triggered by an incident, change or new risk.
Only reviewed when a specific event occurs (e.g. new legislation, major incident).
